member: Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics
message:
As Dr. Marcus Reid, for the rigid core plus mount and power-signal chain:

For F1 conform contact surface and F3 transduce contact stress my field has none for the sensing physics itself — I defer to Dr. Amara Okafor for skin and Prof. Kenji Tanaka for taxels, and I own the core, mount, flex routing and readout they sit on.

Plain words: the fingertip is a hard bone with a soft skin clamped to it that slides into the robot finger like a tool holder and is screwed so grip force goes into the finger, not the skin. The Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) states the design is a rigid core surrounded by an elastic skin filled with liquid to give human fingertip compliance and is rated at forces up to 50 N, the Exploiting High Quality Tactile Sensors for Simplified Grasping (E50) gives the proven 26 by 20 by 25 mm fingertip weighing 9.5 g precedent, and the Installation (E45) shows fingertip holders fastened to finger racks with screws. That means my nail-backed core concept (C21) in the rigid core mount sketch (E54) carries 50.0 N into an M2 screw plus dovetail bracket at 20.0 mm diameter, and the 14.0 g mass budget sum (E53) is about one-and-a-half steel teaspoons and close to the 9.5 g precedent, so everyday finger scale is preserved for Dr. Amara Okafor.

Plain words: the curved sensor flex tails down to a small circuit board on the finger where a converter chip plus a tiny computer turn capacitance into numbers, and the flex connector opens without force so fine traces are not scraped. The AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41) states femtofarad resolution with 13 capacitance sensor inputs at 9 ms update for all 13 inputs, and the FPC Connector Guide : Types and Reliability Considerations (E42) states contacts in ZIF, where ZIF means Zero Insertion Force, connectors have higher cycle rating because they are not rubbed during insertion with 0.5 mm pitch as industry standard. That means the on-finger readout concept (C22) with 0.5 mm ZIF plus FPC, where FPC means Flexible Printed Circuit, and PCB, where PCB means Printed Circuit Board, plus CDC, where CDC means Capacitance-to-Digital Converter, and MCU, where MCU means Microcontroller Unit, preserves Prof. Kenji Tanaka 3.57 fF signal, and the flex needs at least 3.18 mm bend radius per the Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) flex rule requiring at least 1/8 in 3.175 mm radius implemented in the rigid core mount sketch (E54) for Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Plain words: the finger sends a short digital touch message many times per second using little power, like a slow serial text stream. The AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41) runs 2.6 to 3.6 V supply at 1.00 mA full power and 29.0 uA low power mode with SPI, where SPI means Serial Peripheral Interface, compatible interface, matching the Microsoft Word - BioTac Product Manual.docx (E43) 6-pin 5 V SPI precedent. That means the 51.2 kbit per s SPI message rate (E52) at 100 Hz frames is well inside standard SPI megabits per second, and the 0.0991 W fingertip power budget sum (E51) is about one-tenth of a phone charger LED and safe for a fingertip, carrying position from the centroid firmware (C23) plus the 30 ms slip bit (C24) to meet Dr. Elena Vasquez latency rule.

Not ready, because crosstalk of the flex tail across the dovetail joint and 2200 Hz PVDF sampling load on the MCU still need a bench test of continuity under vibration.
